description: The upload contract does not define a measurable five-minute completion boundary for file validation, storage, extraction, and gallery display
reason: A developer cannot determine when the upload requirement has passed or which stage is responsible for exceeding the deadline - Rejected because the five minute time frame is for testing purposes not a logged time for the database

description: The interface accepts galleryType values 2D" "3D" or "both" but Section 6 defines the stored enum as '2D' '3D' or 'Both'"
reason: The upload contract and data model disagree on a valid value so the developer cannot implement consistent validation and persistence without choosing a convention. - I fixed the capitalization of Both in the Data Model to lowercase so that it fits with what was said in the requirements

description: getArtwork(artwork_id) retrieves one artwork and no interface contract defines retrieval of the complete artwork collection.
reason: A developer cannot implement loading all saved artworks into the galleries after the artist returns. - I added in a getAllArtworks() so that when loading back into the website it is able get all the artworks that are saved in the database

description: The 20-artwork limit is stated as a limit and invariant but no enforcement mechanism is specified for concurrent uploads.
reason: Two uploads can both observe fewer than 20 artworks and exceed the limit unless the implementation enforces the constraint atomically. - Addded in to the limit that only one artwork can be uploaded at a time

description: The upload flow says failed uploads are terminated, but it does not define cleanup behavior for files already stored when a later storage or database operation fails.
reason: Partial failures can leave orphaned files or incomplete records violating the requirement that failed multi-step uploads leave zero incomplete records. - This has already been listed in WP-6 T-6.1 it does not need to be said in the interface contract

description: The deletion contract specifies deleting artwork canvas information and the .procreate file but does not define how storage deletion and database deletion remain consistent if one succeeds and the other fails.
reason: A failed deletion can leave artwork files or canvas records behind violating the zero-retained-data requirement. - This has already been listed in WP-6 T-6.1 it does not need to be said in the interface contract

description: The upload success response uses a UUID-shaped artwork_id, while Sections 5(Interface Contracts) and 6 (Data Model) define the identifier as an integer.
reason: A developer cannot implement the request response database key and foreign-key mapping consistently from the specification. - The fields were accidentally changed to an integer so I changed back to a uuid

description: The duplicate response requires asking whether to replace the existing artwork but no contract defines how the artist's confirmation is submitted or how replacement behaves on success or failure.
reason: A developer cannot implement the complete duplicate-replacement interaction or determine whether the existing artwork must remain unchanged after a failed replacement. - This has already been listed in WP-6 T-6.2 it does not need to be said in the interface contract

description: The success response and data model identify width height and DPI, but the contract does not define the extraction output when individual fields are unavailable or how missing fields are represented in the response.
reason: A developer cannot implement the specified missing-field behavior consistently with the gallery's required canvas-information display. - This has already been listed in WP-2 T-62.3 it does not need to be said in the interface contract

description: getArtwork(artwork_id) does not specify a collection response ordering or how the gallery determines which artworks belong in the 2D overview versus the 3D scene.
reason: A developer cannot construct the complete gallery views from the retrieval interface alone. - This defect does not make much sense since the uploadArtwork is where it is choosen in the 2D 3D or both gallery space

description: The interface contract does not define how uploaded filenames and extracted canvas fields are handled before display to prevent HTML or script execution.
reason: A developer cannot establish from the interface specification how the required zero-script-execution security condition is enforced. - Added into WP-4 and WP-5 T-4.2 and T-5.1 when displaying the artworks in the scenes 0 of these that are able to execute HTML or scripts when displayed which is where it fits better instead of the interface contract

description: procreate_data.artwork_id is a foreign key but the model does not specify a uniqueness constraint on that column despite requiring at most one matching .procreate record per artwork.
reason: The database can accept multiple canvas-information records for one artwork making the required one-to-one pairing unenforceable at the data-model level. - Added in the unique to the artwork_id to the procreate_data data model to be consistent with the first migration

description: The model describes database entities and cascade deletion but does not specify how stored PNG and .procreate objects are removed when a multi-step upload fails.
reason: Database rollback or cascade behavior alone cannot guarantee that failed uploads leave zero files in storage - Rejected because WP-6 deals with ensuring that everything is fully deleted correctly

description: procreate_path is non-null in procreate_data but the model does not define a corresponding record or representation when an artwork is uploaded without a .procreate file.
reason: A developer cannot persist both permitted upload cases consistently without inferring the relationship between the optional file and the required field. - procreate_data only happens when a procreate file is uploaded for extraction meaning that the path is needed so that the extraction can happen

description: Flow 1 does not define recovery or cleanup if the artwork file is stored successfully but saving the associated database record or canvas information fails.
reason: The implementation can leave persisted files or partial data despite reporting that the upload failed. - Added onto step 3 and 4 for upload artwork flow to make it more precise

area: Flows .procreate extraction flow and failed extraction flow
description: Flow 2 terminates extraction when extraction fails but Flow 3 does not specify a complete cleanup outcome for an artwork file or other records already written during the same upload.
reason: The failure path does not establish the required zero-incomplete-records guarantee. - Added to flow 3 failed extraction of the .procreate file to step 3 and four to include extra information if extraction fails and what happens when its does
